lessons.title: IP Addresses: The House Numbers
lessons.content_md:
# IP Addresses: The House Numbers 🏠

If you want to send a birthday card to your friend through the mail, what do you need? You need their exact home address.

Computers are exactly the same. When your laptop wants to talk to a Google server to load a YouTube video, it needs to know Google's address. On the internet, this address is called an **IP Address**.

## The Format

An IP (Internet Protocol) address looks like a string of numbers separated by dots. 
For example: `142.250.190.46`

Every single device connected to the internet — your phone, your laptop, your smart TV, and every server in a Data Center — has an IP address. Without it, the internet's delivery trucks (routers) wouldn't know where to send your data!

<flipcard front="🏠 What is an IP Address?" back="An IP Address is a unique string of numbers that acts like a house address for a device on the internet, allowing computers to find and talk to each other."></flipcard>

lessons.title: DNS: The Phonebook of the Web
lessons.content_md:
# DNS: The Phonebook of the Web 📖

We have a problem. Human brains are very bad at remembering random numbers. 

Imagine if, to watch a movie, you had to type `142.250.190.46` into your browser instead of `youtube.com`. You would never remember it!

To solve this, the internet uses **DNS (Domain Name System)**.

## The Magic Translator ✨

DNS is literally the phonebook of the internet. When you open your browser and type `youtube.com`, your computer instantly calls the DNS Phonebook and asks:

> *"Hey DNS, what is the IP address for youtube.com?"*

The DNS Phonebook flips through its pages and replies:

> *"youtube.com is located at 142.250.190.46!"*

Your browser then uses that IP address to connect to the server. This all happens in milliseconds, completely invisibly!

<flipcard front="📖 What does DNS do?" back="DNS translates human-readable names (like google.com) into computer-readable IP addresses (like 142.250.190.46). It's the internet's phonebook!"></flipcard>
